recommended_format.why: Engine DJ recommends exFAT, and every selected player reads it. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700 and XDJ-1000MK2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700 and XDJ-1000MK2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD and OMNIS-DUO.

Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700 and XDJ-1000MK2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-2000NXS2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for that player, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-2000NXS2, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, XDJ-AZ, SC6000 Prime and PRIME 4+.

fixes.detail: Use rekordbox 7.2.11 or later and export to this drive with both Device Library and OneLibrary. BoothReady picks up the new export automatically.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700 and XDJ-1000MK2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-2000NXS2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for that player, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-2000NXS2, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, XDJ-AZ, SC6000 Prime and PRIME 4+.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700 and XDJ-1000MK2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-2000, CDJ-2000NXS and CDJ-2000NXS2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-2000, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-XZ and XDJ-AZ.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700 and XDJ-1000MK2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-2000, CDJ-2000NXS and CDJ-2000NXS2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-2000, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-XZ and XDJ-AZ.

recommended_format.why: You selected equipment that includes the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700 and XDJ-1000MK2. Pioneer DJ documents FAT, FAT32 and HFS+ support for those players, while newer systems also read exFAT. FAT32 gives the selected equipment a common filesystem. The drive gets an MBR partition table, because the GUID partition map macOS uses by default isn't supported by the CDJ-900, CDJ-2000, CDJ-900NXS, CDJ-2000NXS, CDJ-2000NXS2, XDJ-700, XDJ-1000MK2, XDJ-XZ, CDJ-3000, CDJ-3000X, CDJ-1500X, XDJ-AZ, XDJ-AN, OPUS-QUAD, OMNIS-DUO, SC5000 Prime, SC6000 Prime, PRIME 4, PRIME 4+ and SC LIVE 4.

rules.review_note: Checked on 27 September 2026 against AlphaTheta, Pioneer DJ, Denon DJ, Engine DJ and Mixxx documentation and against reports on the Pioneer DJ and Engine DJ community forums. Every vendor or community claim cites its sources below; claims no document covers are marked 'inferred'. MBR support is taken from the documents that confirm FAT32, since they describe MBR-partitioned sticks and name the GUID partition map as the exception. Nothing here is lab verified yet.
